newsitem.title: UK: N Sea crude quiet, traders wait for API's.
newsitem.headline: N Sea crude quiet, traders wait for API's.

text.p: North Sea crude oil markets had another quiet day on Tuesday with levels steady on the day and refiners looking at weaker margins and reluctant to buy, traders said.
"I think people have a lot in tank from the contango market and are slow to buy now the margins have lost ground," one large North Sea producer said.
Brent rose around 80 cents on Monday but products failed to move in line so margins both in the U.S. and Europe lost ground.
Traders waited for tonight's weekly U.S. stock figures from the American Petroleum Institute.

"Fundamentals look weak to me. The pull from the East is less than expected as margins there have fallen and so the West African barrels are looking more to the U.S. We need bullish API's to hold the strength in this market," one said.
All three Brent cargoes from the chains were kept on Tuesday -- one each by Statsco, Shell U.K. and Elf.
Offers of June Brent remained around July -5 cents.
Talk of a late Monday end May Statfjord deal around Dated +25/26 cents was not confirmed but thought around market level.
Oseberg availabilities for June remained ample.
The grade showed little chance of gaining ground from Monday's deal at Dated +15 cents unless a VLCC were to move transAtlantic, traders said.

Late talk on intermonth spreads put June/July at +16/+18 cents, July/Aug at +5/+8 cents and value on the Aug/Sept at +5 cents. The only deals reported were a June/July at +17 cents and an Aug/Dec at +15 cents.
CFD's lost ground over the day with the rest of this week talked around -5/+3 cents, while May 19-23 was talked around evens.
The May 27-30 June 2-6 roll was done on legs at +5 cents while Dated to frontline IPE for June 16-July 15 moved at -12 cents. The average for the month of June traded at July -12 cents.
